a1.he: וְאִילּוּ עַל סְפֵיקוֹ, מֵבִיא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי לָא קָתָנֵי. מַנִּי הָא? אִילֵימָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, לִיתְנֵי נָמֵי סֵיפָא: ״וְעַל סְפֵיקָן מֵבִיא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי״, דְּהָתְנַן: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְחַיֵּיב עַל סְפֵק מְעִילָה אָשָׁם תָּלוּי!

a2.he: אֶלָּא לָאו רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הִיא, וְקָתָנֵי: ״בַּחֲמִשָּׁה הֶעְלֵמוֹת – מֵבִיא חָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת״, וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: קַיבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ!

a3.he: אֶלָּא אַדְּרַבָּה, מִסֵּיפָא, דְּקָתָנֵי: מֵחֲמִשָּׁה זְבָחִים אֲפִילּוּ בְּהֶעְלֵם (אַחַת) [אֶחָד] – חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: לָא קַיבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ!

a4.he: וְאֶלָּא מַאי אִית [לָךְ] לְמֵימַר, תַּנָּאֵי הִיא, דְּאִיכָּא תַּנָּא דְּקַיבְּלַהּ וְאִיכָּא תַּנָּא דְּלָא קַיבְּלַהּ?

a5.he: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא, וְהַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא, סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָתֵיהּ בְּהַעֲלָמָה, וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בִּמְעִילוֹת.

a6.he: הֵיכִי דָמֵי חָמֵשׁ מְעִילוֹת? אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כְּאוֹתָהּ שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ: חֲמִשָּׁה דְּבָרִים בָּעוֹלָה מִצְטָרְפִין: הַבָּשָׂר, וְהֶחָלָב, וְהַיַּיִן, וְהַסֹּלֶת, וְהַשֶּׁמֶן.

a7.he: חִזְקִיָּה אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁאָכַל מֵחֲמִשָּׁה אֵבָרִים. רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בְּאֵבֶר אֶחָד, מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ בְּכָתֵף. רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁאָכַל בַּחֲמִשָּׁה מִינֵי קְדֵירָה. רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁאָכַל בַּחֲמִשָּׁה טְעָמִים.

a8.he: מַתְנִי׳ אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּעוֹשֶׂה מְלָאכוֹת הַרְבֵּה בְּשַׁבָּתוֹת הַרְבֵּה מֵעֵין מְלָאכָה אַחַת בְּהֶעְלֵם (אַחַת) [אֶחָד], מַהוּ? חַיָּיב אַחַת עַל כּוּלָּן, אוֹ חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת?

a9.he: אָמַר לוֹ: חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת, מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר, וּמָה נִדָּה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ תּוֹצָאוֹת הַרְבֵּה וְחַטָּאוֹת הַרְבֵּה – חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת, שַׁבָּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ תּוֹצָאוֹת הַרְבֵּה וּמִיתוֹת הַרְבֵּה – אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁיְּהֵא חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת?

a10.he: אָמַרְתִּי לוֹ: אִם אָמַרְתָּ בַּנִּדָּה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ שְׁתֵּי אַזְהָרוֹת, שֶׁהוּא מוּזְהָר עַל הַנִּדָּה וְהַנִּדָּה מוּזְהֶרֶת עָלָיו, תֹּאמַר בַּשַּׁבָּת, שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ אֶלָּא אַזְהָרָה אֶחָת!

a11.he: אָמַר לִי: הַבָּא עַל הַקְּטַנּוֹת יוֹכִיחַ, שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ אֶלָּא אַזְהָרָה אַחַת, וְחַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת!

a12.he: אָמַרְתִּי לוֹ: אִם אָמַרְתָּ בַּקְּטַנּוֹת, שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן עַכְשָׁיו – יֵשׁ בָּהֶן לְאַחַר זְמַן, תֹּאמַר בַּשַּׁבָּת, שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ עַכְשָׁיו וְלֹא לְאַחַר זְמַן?

a13.he: אָמַר לִי: הַבָּא עַל הַבְּהֵמָה יוֹכִיחַ! אָמַרְתִּי לוֹ: הַבְּהֵמָה כַּשַּׁבָּת.

a14.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי קָבָעֵי מִינֵּיהּ? אִי שַׁבָּתוֹת כְּגוּפִין דָּמְיָין וְאִי לָא בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ, נִיבְעֵי: הָעוֹשֶׂה מְלָאכָה אַחַת בְּשַׁבָּתוֹת הַרְבֵּה!

a15.he: אֶלָּא: וַלְדֵי מְלָאכוֹת אִי כְּאָבוֹת דָּמְיָין וְאִי לָא בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ, נִיבְעֵי מִינֵּיהּ: הָעוֹשֶׂה מְלָאכוֹת הַרְבֵּה מֵעֵין מְלָאכָה אַחַת בַּשַּׁבָּת!

a16.he: אָמַר רָבָא: אָמְרִי בֵּי רַב, תַּרְתֵּי בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ: שַׁבָּתוֹת כְּגוּפִין דָּמְיָין וְאִי לָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ, וַלְדֵי מְלָאכוֹת כִּמְלָאכוֹת דָּמְיָין אִי לָא.

a17.he: וְשַׁבָּתוֹת, הֵיכִי מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ? שִׁגְגַת שַׁבָּת וּזְדוֹן מְלָאכוֹת – פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ דְּיָמִים שֶׁבֵּינְתַיִים הָוְיָין יְדִיעָה לְחַלֵּק,

a18.he: וּזְדוֹן שַׁבָּת וְשִׁגְגַת מְלָאכוֹת הוּא דְּבָעֵי מִינֵּיהּ, אִי כְּגוּפִין דָּמְיָין אִי לָא,

a19.he: אוֹ דִלְמָא, זְדוֹן שַׁבָּת וְשִׁגְגַת מְלָאכוֹת – פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ דִּכְגוּפִין דָּמְיָין, וְשִׁגְגַת שַׁבָּת וּזְדוֹן מְלָאכוֹת הוּא דְּבָעֵי מִינֵּיהּ, דְּיָמִים שֶׁבֵּינָתַיִם אִי הָוְיָין יְדִיעָה לְחַלֵּק אִי לָא?

b1.he: מִסְתַּבְּרָא שִׁגְגַת שַׁבָּת וּזְדוֹן מְלָאכוֹת פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ דְּיָמִים שֶׁבֵּינְתַיִים הָוַיִין יְדִיעָה לְחַלֵּק, וּזְדוֹן שַׁבָּת וְשִׁגְגַת מְלָאכוֹת הוּא דְּבָעֵי מִינֵּיהּ – כְּגוּפִין דָּמְיָין, אוֹ לָאו.

b2.he: וּפְשַׁיט לֵיהּ דִּזְדוֹן שַׁבָּת וְשִׁגְגַת מְלָאכוֹת כְּגוּפִין דָּמְיָין, וְלָא קַבֵּיל מִינֵּיהּ. וּפְשַׁט לֵיהּ, דְּוַלְדֵי מְלָאכוֹת כִּמְלָאכוֹת דָּמְיָין, וְלָא קַבֵּיל מִינֵּיהּ.

b3.he: אָמַר רַבָּה: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דִּתְנַן, כְּלָל גָּדוֹל אָמְרוּ בַּשַּׁבָּת: כׇּל הַשּׁוֹכֵחַ עִיקַּר שַׁבָּת, וְעָשָׂה מְלָאכוֹת הַרְבֵּה בְּשַׁבָּתוֹת הַרְבֵּה – אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת.

b4.he: הַיּוֹדֵעַ עִיקַּר שַׁבָּת, וְעָשָׂה מְלָאכוֹת הַרְבֵּה בְּשַׁבָּתוֹת הַרְבֵּה – חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל שַׁבָּת וְשַׁבָּת. הַיּוֹדֵעַ שֶׁהוּא שַׁבָּת וְעָשָׂה מְלָאכוֹת הַרְבֵּה בְּשַׁבָּתוֹת הַרְבֵּה – חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַב מְלָאכָה וּמְלָאכָה.

b5.he: וְאִילּוּ ״חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַב מְלָאכָה שֶׁל כׇּל שַׁבָּת וְשַׁבָּת״ לָא קָתָנֵי.

b6.he: מַנִּי הָא? אִילֵימָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, אֵימָא סֵיפָא: הָעוֹשֶׂה מְלָאכוֹת הַרְבֵּה מֵעֵין מְלָאכָה אַחַת – אֵין חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אֶחָת, וְאִי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר – חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל וַלְדֵי מְלָאכוֹת כִּמְלָאכוֹת!

b7.he: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא, וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ שִׁגְגַת שַׁבָּת וּזְדוֹן מְלָאכוֹת פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ דְּיָמִים שֶׁבֵּינְתַיִים הָוַיִין יְדִיעָה לְחַלֵּק,

b8.he: זְדוֹן שַׁבָּת וְשִׁגְגַת מְלָאכוֹת הוּא דְּבָעֵי אִי כְּגוּפִין דָּמְיָין, וּפְשַׁט לֵיהּ דִּכְגוּפִין דָּמְיָין, וַלְדֵי מְלָאכוֹת כִּמְלָאכוֹת דָּמְיָין, וְתַרְוַיְיהוּ לָא קַבֵּיל מִינֵּיהּ.

b9.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ זְדוֹן שַׁבָּת וְשִׁגְגַת מְלָאכוֹת פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּשַׁבָּתוֹת לָאו כְּגוּפִין דָּמְיָין, וְשִׁגְגַת שַׁבָּת וּזְדוֹן מְלָאכוֹת הוּא דְּבָעֵי מִינֵּיהּ, דְּיָמִים שֶׁבֵּינְתַיִים מִי הָוַיִין יְדִיעָה לְחַלֵּק אוֹ לָא.

b10.he: וּפְשַׁיט לֵיהּ דְּיָמִים שֶׁבֵּינְתַיִים [הָוַיִין יְדִיעָה] לְחַלֵּק וְקַבֵּיל מִינֵּיהּ, וּפְשַׁט לֵיהּ וַלְדֵי מְלָאכוֹת כִּמְלָאכוֹת דָּמַיִין וְלָא קַבֵּיל מִינֵּיהּ.

b11.he: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: זְדוֹן שַׁבָּת וְשִׁגְגַת מְלָאכוֹת – אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ דִּכְגוּפִין דָּמְיָין, וְכִי בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ, שִׁגְגַת שַׁבָּת וּזְדוֹן מְלָאכוֹת הוּא דְּבָעֵי מִינֵּיהּ, דְּיָמִים שֶׁבֵּינְתַיִים אִי הָוְיָין יְדִיעָה לְחַלֵּק.

b12.he: וּפְשַׁיט לֵיהּ יָמִים שֶׁבֵּינְתַיִים הָוַיִין יְדִיעָה לְחַלֵּק, וְקַבֵּיל מִינֵּיהּ.

b13.he: וּפְשַׁט לֵיהּ דְּוַלְדֵי מְלָאכוֹת כִּמְלָאכוֹת דָּמַיִין, וְלָא קַבֵּיל מִינֵּיהּ.

b14.he: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דְּתַנְיָא: הַכּוֹתֵב שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת בְּהֶעְלֵם אֶחָד – חַיָּיב. בִּשְׁתֵּי הֶעְלֵמוֹת – רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מְחַיֵּיב, וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹטְרִין. וּמוֹדֶה רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, שֶׁאִם כָּתַב אוֹת אַחַת בְּשַׁבָּת זוֹ וְאוֹת אַחַת בְּשַׁבָּת אַחֶרֶת – פָּטוּר.

b15.he: וְתַנְיָא אַחֲרִיתִי: הַכּוֹתֵב שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת בִּשְׁתֵּי שַׁבָּתוֹת, אֶחָד בְּשַׁבָּת זוֹ וְאֶחָד בְּשַׁבָּת זוֹ – רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מְחַיֵּיב, וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹטְרִין. קָא סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ, דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ.

b16.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְדִידִי, דְּאָמֵינָא זְדוֹן שַׁבָּת וְשִׁגְגַת מְלָאכוֹת אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר דְּשַׁבָּתוֹת כְּגוּפִין דָּמְיָין, הָא דְּתַנְיָא פָּטוּר – בִּזְדוֹן שַׁבָּת וְשִׁגְגַת מְלָאכוֹת, דְּשַׁבָּתוֹת כְּגוּפִין דָּמְיָין.

messages.text: Continued from 15b: Rabbi Akiva told Rabbi Yehoshua that his a fortiori inference from misuse of consecrated property to notar could be refuted, and the Gemara asked whether Rabbi Yehoshua accepted the refutation. It cited a baraita: five pieces of notar from one offering, cooked in five pots, eaten during one lapse of awareness, one sin offering; during five lapses, five; from five offerings, liable for each one; Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says even then only one; and five pieces from five pots of one offering eaten before the sprinkling of the blood, a guilt offering for each, due to misuse.
Gemara
And yet in the final case in the baraita, it does not teach that in a situation where he is uncertain whether he ate from it he brings a provisional guilt offering.

notes.dh: ואילו על הספקות כו' לא קתני
notes.he: בסיפא גבי מעילה:
notes.en: And yet for uncertainty etc. it does not teach: in the latter clause, concerning misuse [of consecrated property].

notes.he: של מעילות על ספק אם אכל בה' תמחויין לפני זריקת דמים מביא אשם תלוי [לא] קתני:
notes.en: [A mark in the printed text here reads: up to here belongs to daf 15b.] And yet for their uncertainty: of misuse, for uncertainty whether he ate from the five pots before the sprinkling of the blood, it does [not] teach that he brings a provisional guilt offering.

messages.text: Whose opinion is this? If we say it is the opinion of Rabbi Akiva, let him also teach in the last clause: For a case where he is uncertain whether he ate from them he brings a provisional guilt offering,

notes.he: כלומר ת"ק מני:
notes.en: Whose is this: that is, whose is the first tanna [of the baraita]?

notes.he: סיפא אי נימא ר' עקיבא היא ניתני נמי סיפא כו':
notes.en: Whose is this? The latter clause. If we say it is Rabbi Akiva, let it also teach in the latter clause etc.

messages.text: Rabbi Akiva deems one liable to bring a provisional guilt offering for uncertainty about misuse of consecrated property.

notes.dh: ר"ע מחייב על ספק מעילה כו'
notes.he: בפרק דם שחיטה (לקמן כריתות כב.):
notes.en: Rabbi Akiva deems one liable for uncertain misuse etc.: in the chapter Dam Sheḥita (below, Keritot 22a).

messages.text: Rather, isn’t the baraita in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehoshua, who disagrees with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva and holds that one is not liable to bring a provisional guilt offering for uncertainty about misuse of consecrated property?

notes.he: רישא דברייתא וסיפא וקתני בחמש העלמות מביא ה' חטאות הא ה' חתיכות מזבח אחד בחמש תמחוין בהעלם אחד אינו מביא אלא חטאת אחת:
notes.en: Rather, isn’t it Rabbi Yehoshua: the first clause of the baraita and the latter clause. And it teaches: during five lapses of awareness he brings five sin offerings; hence for five pieces from one offering in five pots during one lapse of awareness, he brings only one sin offering.

messages.text: And it teaches that one who eats notar from one offering cooked in five pots during five separate lapses of awareness brings five sin offerings, which indicates that if he did so during a single lapse of awareness he would be liable to bring only one sin offering, in accordance with the opinion stated by Rabbi Akiva in the mishna. And one can conclude from here that Rabbi Yehoshua accepted the refutation from Rabbi Akiva.

notes.he: העלמות הוא דמחלקין אבל זבחים לא וש"מ הדר ביה ר' יהושע:
notes.en: And it teaches: during five lapses of awareness etc.: it is lapses of awareness that differentiate, but not offerings. And conclude from it that Rabbi Yehoshua retracted.

notes.dh: אלא לאו רבי יהושע היא וקתני בה' העלמות חייב ה' חטאות
notes.he: משום דוקא העלמות מחלקין ופר"י דה"ה דמצי לאתויי מרישא ה' חתיכות מה' תמחויין מזבח אחד אינו חייב אלא אחת דהא במתני' נמי מדמי תמחויין אלא משום דתמחויין לא הוה הבעיא לא נקט ליה:
notes.en: Rather, isn’t it Rabbi Yehoshua, and it teaches: during five lapses of awareness he brings five sin offerings: because specifically lapses of awareness differentiate. And the Ri explains that the same applies: he could have cited the first clause, “five pieces from five pots from one offering, he is liable only one,” since in the mishna too he compares pots. But since pots were not the question, he did not cite it.

notes.he: אלמא קיבלה ר' יהושע להא תשובה מר' עקיבא דאינו מביא אלא חטאת אחת:
notes.en: Evidently Rabbi Yehoshua accepted this refutation from Rabbi Akiva, that he brings only one sin offering.

notes.he: מדקתני רישא חמש חתיכות מזבח אחד בהעלם אחד בה' תמחוין אינו חייב אלא אחת אלמא דלא יליף נותר ממעילה ש"מ קיבלה מיניה:
notes.en: Another version: since the first clause teaches that for five pieces from one offering during one lapse of awareness in five pots he is liable only one, evidently he does not derive notar from misuse. Conclude from it that he accepted it from him.

messages.text: But on the contrary, one can infer otherwise from the latter clause of the baraita, which teaches: If he ate from five separate offerings, even during one lapse of awareness, he is liable to bring a separate sin offering for each and every one. One can conclude from this statement that Rabbi Yehoshua did not accept the refutation from Rabbi Akiva.

notes.he: מצית יליף דלא קיבלה מיניה דקתני [מה'] זבחים חייב על כל אחת ואחת דגופין מוחלקין וה"ה דתמחוין מחלקין אפילו בזבח אחד אלמא יליף נותר ממעילה ש"מ לא קיבלה מיניה:
notes.en: Rather, on the contrary, from the latter clause: you can derive that he did not accept it from him, for it teaches that [from five] offerings he is liable for each one, because the bodies are differentiated; and the same applies that pots differentiate even in one offering. Evidently he derives notar from misuse. Conclude from it that he did not accept it from him.

messages.text: Rather, what is there to say about this baraita? It must be said that it is a dispute between tanna’im, that there is a tanna who maintains that Rabbi Yehoshua accepted Rabbi Akiva’s refutation, and there is a tanna who maintains that Rabbi Yehoshua did not accept it.

notes.he: מיהא ברייתא תנאי היא בתמיה. כלומר מאי בעית למשמע מהך ברייתא תנאי היא ת"ק דקתני העלמות דמשמע דהעלמות מחלקין ולא זבחים אית ליה דקיבלה ר' יהושע והדר ביה והאי דקתני ה' זבחים בהעלם אחד חייב על כל אחד ואחד תנא אחרינא הוא ואית ליה דלא קיבלה אפילו הא לא פשטת מינה דתנאי היא דאפילו תימא ר' עקיבא היא ות"ק אליבא דר"ע קאי מדקתני העלמות דמשמע העלמות ולא זבחים. ודקא קשיא לך דלא תניא אשם תלוי אספק מעילות:
notes.en: Rather, what is there for you to say, that the baraita is a dispute of tanna’im? [This is said] in astonishment. That is: what do you want to understand from this baraita? That it is a dispute of tanna’im: the first tanna, who teaches “lapses of awareness,” implying that lapses differentiate and not offerings, holds that Rabbi Yehoshua accepted it and retracted; and the one who teaches “five offerings during one lapse of awareness, he is liable for each one” is another tanna, who holds that he did not accept it? Even this you have not established from it, that it is a dispute of tanna’im, for you may even say it is Rabbi Akiva, and the first tanna follows Rabbi Akiva, since he teaches “lapses,” implying lapses and not offerings. And as for what troubles you, that it does not teach a provisional guilt offering for uncertain misuse —

notes.dh: אלא מאי אית לך למימר תנאי היא
notes.he: הא דר' יהושע דאיכא תנא דקסבר דקיבלה מיניה וההוא תנא היינו דר' יוסי בר' יהודה ור' שמעון דמתניתין ואיכא תנא דסבר דלא קיבלה מיניה והיינו ת"ק:
notes.en: Rather, what is there for you to say? It is a dispute of tanna’im about this matter of Rabbi Yehoshua: there is a tanna who holds that he accepted it from him, and that tanna is Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, and Rabbi Shimon of our mishna; and there is a tanna who holds that he did not accept it from him, and that is the first tanna.

messages.text: But once the baraita is interpreted in accordance with two different tanna’im, you may even say that the earlier clause of the baraita is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva and not Rabbi Yehoshua.

notes.he: וה' זבחים בהעלם אחת חייב על כל אחת ואחת לאו ר"ע אלא ר' יהושע:
notes.en: You may even say it is Rabbi Akiva: and “five offerings during one lapse of awareness, he is liable for each one” is not Rabbi Akiva but Rabbi Yehoshua.

notes.dh: ואפי' תימא נמי כולה ר' עקיבא
notes.he: לא אמר כולה דוקא דהא קא אבל אכל ה' חתיכות כו'. לא מיתוקמא כר' עקיבא כדאמרן אלא להכי קאמר כולה דבין רישא דברייתא ובין ר' יוסי בר' יהודה הוי כר' עקיבא ומחמשה זבחים מביאין על כל אחת ואחת הא מזבח אחד בחמשה תמחוין אינו מביא אלא אחת היינו נמי כר' עקיבא:
notes.en: And you may even say that all of it is Rabbi Akiva [Rabbeinu Gershom’s text reads “all of it”]: he did not say “all of it” strictly, since the clause “but if he ate five pieces” etc. cannot be established according to Rabbi Akiva, as we said. Rather he says “all of it” because both the first clause of the baraita and Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, follow Rabbi Akiva: from five offerings they bring for each one, whereas from one offering in five pots he brings only one; that too follows Rabbi Akiva.

messages.text: And this tanna of the baraita holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva in one matter and disagrees with his opinion in one matter: He holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva with regard to a lapse of awareness, that if one eats from five offerings during a single lapse of awareness he is liable to bring only one sin offering. But he disagrees with his opinion with regard to misuse of consecrated property, as he does not deem one liable to bring a provisional guilt offering for uncertainty about whether he misused consecrated property.

notes.he: והאי דקתני מה' זבחים בהעלם אחד חייב על כל אחד תנא אחרינא הוא ור' יהושע היא:
notes.en: This tanna holds like him etc.: and the one who teaches “from five offerings during one lapse of awareness he is liable for each one” is another tanna, and it is Rabbi Yehoshua.

notes.he: והאי תנא נמי דאבל אכל נמי ר' עקיבא אלא דסבר לה כוותיה בחדא ופליג עליה בחדא:
notes.en: And this tanna of “but if he ate” is also Rabbi Akiva, except that he holds like him in one matter and disagrees with him in one matter.

notes.he: סבר לה כוותיה בחדא בהעלמות דנותר מזבח אחד בחמש תמחוין דאינו מביא אלא אחת:
notes.en: He holds like him in one matter: in lapses of awareness, that for notar from one offering in five pots he brings only one.

notes.he: במעילה וספק מעילות דלא תנא ועל ספיקן מביא אשם תלוי על כל אחת ואחת:
notes.en: And disagrees with him: on misuse and uncertain misuse, since he does not teach: “And for their uncertainty he brings a provisional guilt offering for each one.”

messages.text: § The mishna teaches that if one eats five pieces from a single offering, each of which was cooked in a separate pot, he is liable to bring five guilt offerings for misuse of consecrated property. What are the circumstances which require five guilt offerings for misuse of consecrated property?

notes.he: היכי דמי ה' תמחוין דכי אכלן בה' תמחוין דחייב:
notes.en: What are the circumstances of five pots, such that when he ate them in five pots he is liable?

messages.text: The five pieces must be from separate parts of the offering, like that which we learned in a mishna with regard to a different topic:

notes.dh: אמר שמואל כאותה ששנינו ה' דברים בעולה מצטרפין הבשר החלב והיין והסולת והשמן
notes.he: היין והסולת והשמן היינו נסכין ומנחה שקריבין עם העולה ומדאיצטריך למימר דמצטרפין לכזית לחיוב ש"מ דכל אחד תמחוי בפני עצמו מאכל בפני עצמן הן דאי אכל מכל חד כזית דחייב חמשה דאי לא הוויין ה' תמחויין לא איצטריך למימר דמצטרפין דפשיטא דמצטרפין:
notes.en: Shmuel says: Like that which we learned: Five items in a burnt offering combine: the meat, the fat, the wine, the fine flour and the oil. The wine, the fine flour and the oil are the libations and the meal offering brought with the burnt offering. And since it was necessary to state that they combine to an olive-bulk for liability, conclude from it that each one is a separate pot, a food in its own right, so that if he ate an olive-bulk from each one he is liable five times. For if they were not five pots, there would be no need to say that they combine, since it would be obvious that they combine.

messages.text: Five items from a burnt offering combine to form an olive-bulk that renders one liable for sacrificing an offering outside the Temple: The meat, and the forbidden fat, and the wine from the libations of the burnt offering, and the fine flour from the meal offering brought with the libations, and the oil for mixing with the meal offering.

notes.he: לענין כזית להעלותן בחוץ שאם העלן חייב כרת ולהכי נקט עולה דבשאר זבחים לא מצטרף בשר לפי שאינן כליל. כאותה ששנינו כו' ה"נ שאכל מה' דברים הללו:
notes.en: Five items in a burnt offering combine: with regard to an olive-bulk for offering them up outside [the Temple], for if he offered them up he is liable to karet. And that is why it mentions a burnt offering, since in other offerings the meat does not combine, because they are not burnt whole. “Like that which we learned” etc.: here too, he ate from these five items.

messages.text: The obligation to bring five guilt offerings applies in a case where he ate from five different limbs of one offering.

notes.he: אפי' תימא בעולה עצמה בלא יין וסולת ושמן משכחת בה' תמחוין כגון שאכל מה' אברים של עולה חשיב ה' תמחוין:
notes.en: Ḥizkiyya says: you may even say that in the burnt offering itself, without the wine, fine flour and oil, you find five pots: for example, he ate from five limbs of the burnt offering; it counts as five pots.

messages.text: You may even say that he ate from one limb, and you find this in a case where he ate from the shoulder of an offering, which has several different sections.

notes.he: יש ה' אברים הפרסה והעצם התחתון עד הארכובה ושני עצמות לבד מן הכתף:
notes.en: In the shoulder: there are five limbs [in it]: the hoof, and the lower bone up to the knee joint, and two bones, apart from the shoulder [itself].

notes.he: יש בה ז' עצמות:
notes.en: In the shoulder of a burnt offering: it has seven bones.

notes.dh: ריש לקיש אמר אפילו באבר אחד
notes.he: משכחת לה ה' תמחוין בכתף דיש בו ה' עצמות אחד פס רגל היד והשני עצם השוק שעליו והשלישי העצם הזרוע שניתן לכהנים והרביעי היא העצם שקורין עגול הוא שעל גביו והחמישי הוא כף הכתף:
notes.en: Reish Lakish says: even in one limb you find five pots, in the shoulder, which has five bones: the first, the flat of the foreleg; the second, the shank bone above it; the third, the foreleg bone that is given to the priests; the fourth, the bone called “round,” which is on top of it; and the fifth, the shoulder blade.

messages.text: It applies in a case where he ate pieces of meat prepared as five different types of cooked dishes.

notes.he: כגון כרישין ובצלים וכרוב ודלעת ולפת ואכלן כזה עצמו וכזה עצמו:
notes.en: Five kinds of pot dishes: for example leeks, onions, cabbage, gourd and turnip, and he ate [meat cooked] with this one by itself and with that one by itself.

notes.he: פר"י כגון צלי ומבושל וטיגון וצלי קדר וכבוש וה' מיני טעמים כגון פילפלין וזנגבילא וקנה וקנמון וקדה ורש"י לא פירש כן:
notes.en: In five kinds of pot dishes: the Ri explains, for example roasted, cooked, fried, pot-roasted and pickled; and five kinds of flavors, for example pepper, ginger, [aromatic] cane, cinnamon and cassia. And Rashi did not explain it so.

notes.dh: כגון שאכל אפילו חד אבר בה' מיני קדירה
notes.he: כגון מקצת אחד עם כרישין ומקצת אחד עם כרוב ומקצת אחד עם לפתות ומקצת עם תרדין ומקצתן עם קטנית:
notes.en: For example, he ate even one limb in five kinds of pot dishes: for example, part of it with leeks, part with cabbage, part with turnips, part with beets and part with legumes.

messages.text: It applies in a case where he ate five pieces of meat that had five different flavors, as they were prepared with different types of seasonings.

notes.he: צלי ומבושל כבוש שלוק וצלי קדר:
notes.en: Five kinds of flavors: roasted, cooked, pickled, well-boiled, and pot-roasted.

notes.he: כגון צלי ומבושל ושלוק ומתובל ומטוגן:
notes.en: In five kinds of flavors: for example roasted, cooked, well-boiled, seasoned and fried.

messages.text: Mishna

I asked Rabbi Eliezer with regard to one who performs multiple prohibited labors on several Shabbatot, and all those labors were subsumed as subcategories of one primary category of prohibited labor, and he performed them during one lapse of awareness. What is the halakha? Is he liable to bring one sin offering for unwitting performance of all these labors or is he liable to bring a sin offering for violation of each and every one of the labors?

notes.dh: מתני' מלאכות הרבה מעין מלאכה אחת
notes.he: תולדות הרבה של אב אחד בשבתות הרבה אותן שעשה בשבת זו עשה בשבתות אחריני וכולן בהעלם אחת. ובגמרא פריך מאי קמבעיא ליה דנקט תרי מילי שבתות הרבה ותולדות הרבה ואמאי נקט תולדות ולא אבות:
notes.en: Mishna: Many labors of the type of one labor: many subcategories of one primary category, on many Shabbatot: those he performed on this Shabbat he performed on other Shabbatot, and all of them during one lapse of awareness. And in the Gemara it asks: What is his dilemma, that he mentions two things, many Shabbatot and many subcategories? And why does he mention subcategories and not primary categories?

notes.dh: העושה מלאכות הרבה בשבתות הרבה מעין מלאכה אחת
notes.he: היינו כגון אב ותולדותיו או שעשה תולדות של אב מלאכה אחת היינו מעין מלאכה אחת:
notes.en: One who performs many labors on many Shabbatot of the type of one labor: that is, for example, a primary category and its subcategories, or he did subcategories of one primary labor; that is “of the type of one labor.”

messages.text: He is liable to bring a sin offering for violation of each and every one of the labors, and this is derived from an a fortiori inference:

notes.he: עניינים הרבה כגון שבת דאיכא אבות מלאכות ותולדותיהן:
notes.en: Many outcomes: many matters, as with Shabbat, where there are primary categories of labor and their subcategories.

messages.text: Just as in the case of a menstruating woman, with regard to whom there are not multiple actions that result in transgression and that result in multiple sin offerings, but rather only the prohibition against engaging in intercourse with her, and nevertheless one is liable to bring a separate sin offering for each and every one of his acts of unwitting intercourse; in the case of Shabbat, with regard to which there are multiple primary categories and subcategories of labor that result in transgression and that result in multiple death penalties or sin offerings, is it not right that he will be liable to bring a sin offering for performance of each and every one of the prohibited labors?

notes.he: דאין חיובה אלא ביאה וחייב על כל ביאה וביאה בהעלם אחת כדאמר ר"א לעיל בגמרא בא עליה וחזר ובא עליה כו':
notes.en: A menstruating woman, with whom there are not many outcomes: for the liability with her is only for intercourse, and he is liable for each act of intercourse during one lapse of awareness, as Rabbi Eliezer said above in the Gemara: he engaged in intercourse with her and again engaged in intercourse with her etc.

notes.he: כלומר מה אם הנדה שאין בה תוצאות הרבה לחטאות הרבה היינו שאין בה עניינין הרבה של אבות מלאכות לחייבו חטאות הרבה ואין לה תולדות אין בה אלא חיוב ביאה בלבד ואעפ"כ חייב על כל ביאה וביאה שבת שיש בה תוצאות הרבה לחטאות כגון ל"ט אבות מלאכות ותולדות דאין מספר:
notes.en: And just as a menstruating woman, who has not etc.: that is, if with a menstruating woman, who has not many outcomes for many sin offerings, meaning she has not many matters like the primary labors to make him liable to many sin offerings, and has no subcategories, but only the liability for intercourse, and even so he is liable for each act of intercourse; then Shabbat, which has many outcomes for sin offerings, such as the thirty-nine primary labors and subcategories without number, [is it not right that he be liable for each one]?

messages.text: I said to Rabbi Eliezer that the inference is not valid: If you said one is liable to bring multiple sin offerings in the case of a menstruating woman, with regard to whom there are two prohibitions, as the man is prohibited from engaging in intercourse with the menstruating woman and the menstruating woman is prohibited from engaging in intercourse with him, would you say the same in the case of Shabbat, with regard to which there is only one prohibition?

notes.he: דכתיב (ויקרא כ׳:י״ח) ונכרתו שניהם מקרב עמם:
notes.en: And the menstruating woman is prohibited regarding him: as it is written: “And both of them shall be cut off from among their people” (Leviticus 20:18).

notes.he: תאמר בשבת שאין בה אלא אזהרה אחת שהוא מוזהר על השבת בלבד ואין השבת מוזהר עליו:
notes.en: Would you say the same of Shabbat, which has only one prohibition: that he is prohibited regarding Shabbat alone, but Shabbat is not prohibited regarding him.

messages.text: The halakha of one who engages in intercourse with minor menstruating girls will prove this refutation is not valid, as in that case there is only one prohibition, because the minor is exempt from the mitzvot, and nevertheless the man is liable to bring a separate sin offering for intercourse for each and every one of the acts of intercourse.

notes.he: כמו על הקטנה ומאי קטנות דעלמא. כלומר הבא על אחת מן הקטנות ביאות הרבה בנדתה יוכיח שאינה מוזהרת עליו וחייב על כל ביאה וביאה:
notes.en: With minor girls: like “with a minor girl”; and what are “minor girls”? Minor girls in general. That is: one who engages in intercourse many times with one of the minor girls during her menstruation will prove it, since she is not prohibited regarding him, and he is liable for each act of intercourse.

notes.dh: (אמר לו הבא על הקטנות נדות יוכיח שאין בה אלא אזהרה אחת
notes.he: שהוא מוזהר עליהן והן אין דעדיין ק' בלבד ואין השבת מוזהרת עליו):
notes.en: (He said to him: One who engages in intercourse with minor girls who are menstruating will prove it, as there is only one prohibition: that he is prohibited regarding them, and they are not, since they are still minors, alone; and Shabbat is not prohibited regarding him.) [The printed text sets this line in parentheses; the next note gives it in full.]

notes.he: א"ל הבא על הקטנות נדות יוכיח שאין בהן אלא אזהרה אחת שהן מוזהרין עליהן והן אין מוזהרות עליו דעדיין קטנות הן ואינן בנות אזהרות ואעפ"כ חייב על כל אחת ואחת:
notes.en: He said to him: One who engages in intercourse with minor girls who are menstruating will prove it, as there is only one prohibition with them: he is prohibited regarding them, but they are not prohibited regarding him, since they are still minors and not subject to prohibitions. And even so he is liable for each one.

messages.text: I said to Rabbi Eliezer that the cases of Shabbat and minor menstruating girls are not comparable. If you said in the case of minor girls that although it is not prohibited for them at present it is prohibited for them after the passage of time, when they reach majority, would you say the same in the case of Shabbat, with regard to which there are neither two prohibitions at present, nor will there be after the passage of time?

notes.dh: אע"פ שאין בהן עכשיו אזהרה יש בה לאחר זמן
notes.he: כשהן גדולות יש בהן ב' אזהרות תאמר בשבת כו':
notes.en: Although they have no prohibition now, they have one after time: when they are grown, they have two prohibitions. Would you say the same of Shabbat etc.

messages.text: The halakha of one who copulates with an animal will prove this refutation is not valid, as there are never two prohibitions in that case, and nevertheless the person is liable to bring a sin offering for each and every act.

notes.he: שחייב על כל ביאה כדאמרן לעיל טעמא שא"א לערב הביאות:
notes.en: One who copulates with an animal will prove it: that he is liable for each act, as we said above, the reason being that it is impossible to combine the acts.

notes.he: שאין בה אלא אזהרה אחת בלבד שהוא מוזהר על הבהמה והבהמה אינה מוזהרת ואעפ"כ חייב עליה על כל ביאה וביאה אף אני אביא שבת:
notes.en: One who copulates with an animal will prove it: as there is only one prohibition, for he is prohibited regarding the animal but the animal is not prohibited; and even so he is liable for each act. So too I will bring [the same reasoning to] Shabbat.

messages.text: I said to Rabbi Eliezer that no proof can be cited from the case of an animal, as in my opinion the case of the animal is like that of Shabbat; there is uncertainty with regard to both cases.

notes.he: פלוגתא היא בגמרא איכא למאן דאמר קבל ר"ע מר"א והכי קאמר ליה בהמה כשבת מה בהמה חייב על כל אחת ואחת אף שבת חייב על כל אחת דאינו יודע להשיב כלום ולמאן דאמר לא קיבלה מיניה ה"ק ליה אף בהמה מיבעי לי כשבת:
notes.en: The animal is like Shabbat: this is a dispute in the Gemara. According to the one who says Rabbi Akiva accepted it from Rabbi Eliezer, this is what he said to him: the animal is like Shabbat; just as with an animal he is liable for each one, so too with Shabbat he is liable for each one, for he did not know how to reply at all. And according to the one who says he did not accept it from him, this is what he said to him: about the animal too I am uncertain, as with Shabbat.

notes.he: אמרתי לו בהמה כשבת כלומר בהמה דאין לו בה אלא באזהרה אחת מיבעיא לי נמי כמו שבת אי חייב אחת על ביאות הרבה או על כל אחת ואחת:
notes.en: I said to him: The animal is like Shabbat. That is: about the animal, where he has only one prohibition, I am also uncertain, as with Shabbat, whether he is liable once for many acts or for each one.

messages.text: Gemara
What precise dilemma did Rabbi Akiva raise before Rabbi Eliezer?

notes.he: דנקט שבתות הרבה ועושה בזו אותה מלאכה שעשה בזו ונקט תולדות ולא אבות:
notes.en: Gemara: What did he ask of him: that he mentions many Shabbatot, performing on this one the same labor he performed on that one, and mentions subcategories and not primary categories.

messages.text: If he raised a dilemma about whether different Shabbatot are comparable to separate entities or not, i.e., if performing one labor on several Shabbatot during one lapse of awareness is similar to engaging in intercourse with multiple menstruating women during one lapse of awareness, let him raise the dilemma as follows: If one performs one prohibited labor on each of several Shabbatot during a single lapse of awareness, what is the halakha?

notes.dh: אי קבעי מיניה שבתות כגופין דמיין אי לא
notes.he: אי האי דעבד בכמה שבתות אותן מלאכות שעשה בזו עשה בזו ובהעלם אחד דלא הודע לו בינתיים מי אמרינן כיון דבתרי שבתות עשאן הויין הני תרתי שבתות כשני גופי עבירות כאילו קצר וזרע בהעלם אחת וחייב על כל אחת או לא דאמרינן דהוי כעושה מלאכה אחת כמה פעמים בהעלם אחת דחייב חדא אי הא קמיבעיא ליה אמאי נקט תולדות ליבעי הכי אעשה אב מלאכה אחת בשבתות הרבה מהו:
notes.en: If he was asking him whether Shabbatot are like separate entities or not: if this one, who on several Shabbatot performed on this one the same labors he performed on that one, during one lapse of awareness, without it becoming known to him in between: do we say that since he performed them on two Shabbatot, these two Shabbatot are like two separate bodies of transgression, as though he reaped and sowed during one lapse of awareness, where he is liable for each one; or not, but rather we say it is like one who performs one labor several times during one lapse of awareness, who is liable only once? If this is what he was uncertain about, why does he mention subcategories? Let him ask it this way: one who performs one primary labor on many Shabbatot, what is [the law]?

notes.he: מאי קא מיבעיא ליה לר' עקיבא אי שבתות הרבה כחילוק גופין של נדה דמיין לחייבו על כל שבת ושבת כמו הבא על נדות הרבה שחייב על כל נדה ונדה:
notes.en: What was Rabbi Akiva uncertain about? Whether many Shabbatot are like the differentiated bodies of menstruating women, so as to make him liable for each Shabbat, just as one who engages in intercourse with many menstruating women is liable for each one.

notes.he: א"כ ניבעי מיניה העושה מלאכה אחת בשבתות הרבה דומיא דנדה דמלאכה אחת היא:
notes.en: If so, let him ask him about one who performs one labor on many Shabbatot, similar to the menstruating woman, since it is one labor.

messages.text: Rather, perhaps he raised a dilemma about whether different subcategories of a single prohibited labor are comparable to different primary categories, which would mean one is liable separately for each, or not. But if so, let him ask raise the dilemma in the following manner: In the case of one who performs multiple prohibited labors, all subsumed as subcategories of one primary category of labor, on a single Shabbat, during a single lapse of awareness, what is the halakha? Why did Rabbi Akiva specify a case of one who performed multiple prohibited labors on multiple Shabbatot?

notes.he: אם עושה תולדות הרבה מאב אחד אי חייב אחת או על כל אחת ואחת ולהכי נקט תולדות אם כן אמאי נקט שבתות הרבה ליבעי הכי העושה מלאכות הרבה מעין מלאכה אחת בשבת אחת:
notes.en: If he was asking him about offshoots of labors: if one performs many subcategories of one primary category, whether he is liable one or for each one, and that is why he mentions subcategories. If so, why does he mention many Shabbatot? Let him ask it this way: one who performs many labors of the type of one labor on one Shabbat.

notes.he: לחייב עליהן כאבות מלאכות ואי לא קא בעי מיניה משום הכי קאמר מעין מלאכה א"כ ניבעי מיניה העושה מלאכות הרבה תולדות מעין מלאכה אחת בשבת אחת ואמאי קאמר בשבתות הרבה:
notes.en: Whether offshoots of labors are like labors, so as to make him liable for them as for primary labors, or not, is what he asked him, and that is why he said “of the type of one labor.” If so, let him ask him about one who performs many labors, subcategories of the type of one labor, on one Shabbat. Why does he say “on many Shabbatot”?

messages.text: They say in the school of Rav [bei Rav] that Rabbi Akiva raised two dilemmas before him: He raised a dilemma about whether Shabbatot are comparable to separate entities or whether they are not comparable to separate entities, and he also raised a dilemma about whether different subcategories of a single prohibited labor are comparable to different primary categories of labor, or whether they are not.

notes.he: ופשיט תרוייהו לחומרא מדקתני חייב על כל אחת ואחת ואע"ג דמנדה לא מצי למיפשט ליה אלא חדא דהא בנדה ליכא תולדות:
notes.en: He asked him two things: and he resolved both of them stringently, since it teaches “liable for each and every one,” even though from the menstruating woman he could resolve only one of them for him, since with a menstruating woman there are no subcategories.

notes.he: תרתי בעא מיניה והכא מתרצי לבעיא דידיה העושה (מעין) מלאכה אחת בשבתות הרבה היינו אי כגופין דמיין או העושה מלאכות הרבה מעין מלאכה אחת אפילו בשבת אחת בהעלם אחת. היינו אי וולדי מלאכות כמלאכות דמיין:
notes.en: He asked him two things, and here they explain his question: one who performs one labor on many Shabbatot, that is, whether they are like separate bodies; and one who performs many labors of the type of one labor even on one Shabbat during one lapse of awareness, that is, whether offshoots of labors are like labors.

messages.text: Rabbi Eliezer answered that multiple Shabbatot are comparable to separate entities, and that one who performs different subcategories of a single category of prohibited labor is like one who performs multiple primary categories of labor.

notes.dh: ופשט ליה דשבתות כי גופין דמיין
notes.he: מנדה מה אם בנדה אחת חייב על כל ביאה וביאה כ"ש על ביאות של נדות הרבה דגופין מוחלקין דחייב על כל אחת ואחת. אף שבתות נמי כי גופין דמיין:
notes.en: [A mark in the printed text here reads: up to here belongs to daf 16a.] And he resolved for him that Shabbatot are like bodies, from the menstruating woman: if with one menstruating woman he is liable for each act of intercourse, all the more so with acts of intercourse with many menstruating women, whose bodies are differentiated, he is liable for each one. So too Shabbatot are like bodies.

notes.dh: ופשט ליה דוולדי מלאכות כמלאכות דמיין
notes.he: מדקאמר ומה נדה שאין בה תוצאות הרבה הא אי הוו בה תוצאות הרבה הוה חייב על כל מין ומין אף בשבת דיש בה תולדות ליחייב על תולדה כעל אב:
notes.en: And he resolved for him that offshoots of labors are like labors: since he said “And just as a menstruating woman, who has not many outcomes,” it follows that had she many outcomes he would be liable for each kind. So too with Shabbat, which has subcategories, let him be liable for a subcategory as for a primary labor.

messages.text: And in connection to the performance of the same category of prohibited labor on each of several Shabbatot during a single lapse of awareness, what is the precise case about which Rabbi Akiva raises his dilemma?

notes.he: כלומר אי בשגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות או בזדון שבת ושגגת מלאכה. אי שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות דאינו חייב על כל מלאכות של כל שבת ושבת אלא אחת הואיל וזדון מלאכות:
notes.en: And Shabbat, how was he uncertain? That is, whether with unwitting Shabbat and intentional labors, or with intentional Shabbat and unwitting labor. If unwitting Shabbat and intentional labors, where he is liable not for all the labors of each Shabbat but only once, since the labors were intentional,

messages.text: If the individual was unwitting in that he was unaware that it was Shabbat but acted intentionally with regard to the prohibited labors, i.e., he knew that these labors are prohibited on Shabbat, perhaps it is obvious to Rabbi Akiva that the intervening days constitute an awareness of his sin, which serves to differentiate between the Shabbatot and render the individual liable to bring separate sin offerings for each Shabbat.

notes.he: איזו מהן כלומר ה"ד דקעביד לה להא (אב) מלאכה בכמה שבתות בשגגת שבתות וזדון מלאכות פשיטא ליה לר"ע דחייב על כל אחת דלא אמרינן חדא שגגה אלא אמרינן ימים שבינתיים הויין ידיעה דדמי כמי שנודע לו בינתיים דשבת הוי והוי כעושה מלאכה אחת בכמה העלמות:
notes.en: And Shabbatot, how: which of them? That is, what are the circumstances in which he performs this (primary) labor on several Shabbatot? With unwitting Shabbat and intentional labors, it is obvious to Rabbi Akiva that he is liable for each one, for we do not say it is one error; rather we say that the intervening days are awareness, as if it had become known to him in between that it was Shabbat, and it is like one who performs one labor during several lapses of awareness.

notes.dh: ופשיטא ליה דימים של חול שבינתים שבין של כל שבת ושבת הויין ידיעה לחלק לחטאות
notes.he: אע"ג דבהעלם אחד הן:
notes.en: it is obvious to him that the weekdays in between, between each Shabbat, are awareness to differentiate for sin offerings, even though they are during one lapse of awareness.

messages.text: And if so, it is in reference to a case where the individual acts intentionally with regard to Shabbat, i.e., he knows that it is Shabbat, but he acts unwittingly in that he does not know that the prohibited labors he is performing are prohibited on Shabbat, that Rabbi Akiva raises his dilemma.

notes.he: יודע שהוא שבת ושגגת מלאכות דסבור שמלאכה זו מותרת היא דבעי מיניה דהא ליכא למימר ימים שבינתיים הויין ידיעה לחלק דלהכי הויין ידיעה לידע ששבת היתה אבל לענין שגגת מלאכות ליכא ידיעה עד שילמוד והכי קמיבעיא ליה האי דעבד חדא מלאכה בב' שבתות מי אמרינן כיון דבב' ימים הם אף על גב דהעלם אחד הוא לגבי מלאכות הויין הנך שבתות כגופין של מלאכה שאינן דומין זה לזה כגון זרע וקצר בהעלם אחד בזדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות דחייב על כל אחת כדאמרינן שבת (דף ע.) אחת שהיא הנה זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות:
notes.en: And intentional Shabbat: he knows that it is Shabbat, and unwitting labors, thinking this labor is permitted: that is what he asked him. For here one cannot say that the intervening days are awareness to differentiate, because they serve as awareness for knowing that it was Shabbat, but with regard to being unwitting about labors there is no awareness until he learns. And this is what he was uncertain about: this one who performed one labor on two Shabbatot, do we say that since they are on two days, even though it is one lapse of awareness with regard to the labors, these Shabbatot are like separate bodies of labor that are not similar to one another, as when one sowed and reaped during one lapse of awareness with intentional Shabbat and unwitting labors, where he is liable for each one, as we say in Shabbat (70a): “One” that is “many”: intentional Shabbat and unwitting labors?

notes.he: היינו בהעלם אחת:
notes.en: But intentional Shabbat and unwitting labors: that is, during one lapse of awareness,

messages.text: His dilemma is whether the Shabbatot are comparable to separate entities, which would mean that he is liable to bring a separate sin offering for each Shabbat, or whether they are not comparable to separate entities and therefore he is liable to bring only one sin offering.

notes.he: כגופין דמיין והרי עשה בהעלם אחד מלאכה אחת י' פעמים שאינו חייב אלא אחת:
notes.en: Or not: [they are not] like separate bodies, and he has performed one labor ten times during one lapse of awareness, for which he is liable only once.

notes.dh: ובעי מיניה אי שבתות כגופין דמיין
notes.he: לחלק לחייבו על כל שבת ושבת ועל כל אב מלאכה ומלאכה הואיל והעלם מלאכות בידו אי לא:
notes.en: and he asked him whether Shabbatot are like bodies, so as to differentiate and make him liable for each Shabbat and for each primary labor, since unawareness of the labors is in his hand, or not.

messages.text: Or perhaps in the case where he acts intentionally with regard to Shabbat and unwittingly with regard to prohibited labors, it is obvious to Rabbi Akiva that the Shabbatot are comparable to separate entities and he is liable to bring a separate sin offering for each Shabbat.

notes.he: או דלמא זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות פשיטא ליה לר' עקיבא דשבתות כגופין דמיין הואיל דאיכא חילוק חטאות ומלאכות דבשגגת מלאכות חייב על כל מלאכה ומלאכה ה"ה הכי איכא חילוק שבתות וכגופין דמיין וחייב על כל שבת ושבת:
notes.en: Or perhaps with intentional Shabbat and unwitting labors it is obvious to Rabbi Akiva that Shabbatot are like bodies: since there is a differentiation of sin offerings and labors, for with unwitting labors he is liable for each labor, so too there is a differentiation of Shabbatot, and they are like bodies, and he is liable for each Shabbat.

messages.text: And it is in reference to a case where he acts unwittingly in that he does not know it is Shabbat, but he acts intentionally in that he knows that the labors he is performing are prohibited on Shabbat, that Rabbi Akiva raises his dilemma. His dilemma is whether the intervening days between the Shabbatot are considered awareness of his sin, which would serve to differentiate between one sin and the next, or not.

notes.dh: או דלמא זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות פשיטא ליה דשבתות
notes.he: כגופי מלאכות שאין דומות זו לזו שהעושן בשגגת מלאכות וזדון שבת חייב שתים דהיינו אחת שהיא הנה ובשגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות קמבעיא ליה דאפילו אמרי' כגופין דמיין לא מחייב אלא חדא דהיינו הנה שהיא אחד שהעושה ב' אבות בשגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות בהעלם אחד אינו חייב אלא אחת אלא אי איכא ידיעה בינתיים דשבת היא מהניא לחלק דהעלמות מחלקין והכי קמיבעיא ליה מי אמרינן ימים שבנתיים הויין ידיעה כמו שנודע לו ששבת היא אי לא:
notes.en: Or perhaps, with intentional Shabbat and unwitting labors, it is obvious to him that Shabbatot are like separate bodies of labors that are not similar to one another, so that one who performs them unwitting about labors and intentional about Shabbat is liable twice, which is “one that is many”; and it is with unwitting Shabbat and intentional labors that he was uncertain. For even if we say they are like separate bodies, he would be liable only once, as that is “many that are one,” since one who performs two primary labors with unwitting Shabbat and intentional labors during one lapse of awareness is liable only once, unless there is awareness in between that it is Shabbat, which serves to differentiate, since lapses of awareness differentiate. And this is what he was uncertain about: do we say that the intervening days are awareness, like one who was made aware that it is Shabbat, or not?

notes.he: ושגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות כיון דאינו חייב אלא אחת על כל המלאכות הוא דבעי מיניה דימים של בינתים כיון דשגג שבתות הרבה בהעלם אחת מי הוויין ימים שבינתים שבין שבת לשבת ידיעה לחלק אי לא אמר רבא מסתברא דשגגת שבת כו':
notes.en: And with unwitting Shabbat and intentional labors, since he is liable only once for all the labors, that is what he asked him: since he was unwitting about many Shabbatot during one lapse of awareness, are the days in between, between one Shabbat and the next, awareness to differentiate or not? Rava said [so Rabbeinu Gershom; the daf reads Rabba]: It stands to reason that unwitting Shabbat etc.

messages.text: …It stands to reason, based on a proof from a mishna, to say that in a case where he acts unwittingly in that he does not know that it is Shabbat, and intentionally in that he knows that the labors he is performing are prohibited on Shabbat, it is obvious to Rabbi Akiva that the intervening days between the Shabbatot are considered awareness of his sin, which would serve to differentiate between one sin and the next.

notes.he: מהא מתני' דאמרינן לקמן:
notes.en: It stands to reason: from the mishna that we cite below.

messages.text: And it is in reference to a case where he acts intentionally with regard to Shabbat and unwittingly with regard to prohibited labors that Rabbi Akiva raises his dilemma, which is about whether the Shabbatot are comparable to separate entities or not.

And Rabbi Eliezer resolved his dilemma for him by stating that in a case where he acts intentionally with regard to Shabbat and unwittingly with regard to prohibited labors, the Shabbatot are comparable to separate entities. But Rabbi Akiva did not accept this resolution from him.

notes.he: ופשט ליה דשבתות כי גופין דמיין כו'. ואם תאמר קשיא מיניה אדרבה שהרי רבה קאמר לעיל לר"א דקצר וקצר מחייב תרתי אפי' בשבת אחת וא"כ למה צריך שבתות כגופין דמיין וכן בנדה מאי נפקא ליה מיניה מגופין מוחלקין הא ר"א מחייב על כל ביאה וביאה וי"ל דר"א השיב לר"ע לפי דברי רבי עקיבא:
notes.en: Rabba said: It stands to reason etc., and he resolved for him that Shabbatot are like separate entities etc. And if you will say: on the contrary, there is a difficulty from Rabba himself, for Rabba said earlier that according to Rabbi Eliezer one who reaped and reaped again is liable twice even on one Shabbat. If so, why does he need Shabbatot to be like separate entities? And likewise with the menstruating woman, what does he gain from differentiated bodies, since Rabbi Eliezer deems one liable for each act of intercourse? One can say that Rabbi Eliezer answered Rabbi Akiva according to Rabbi Akiva’s own view.

messages.text: And with regard to Rabbi Akiva’s other dilemma, Rabbi Eliezer resolved it for him by stating that subcategories of labors are comparable to primary categories of labor, and one is liable to bring a separate sin offering for each act. But Rabbi Akiva did not accept this resolution from him either.
From where do I say this? As we learned in a mishna:

notes.he: דזדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות בעא מיניה אי כגופין דמיין ופשט ליה דכגופין דמיין דחייב על כל שבת ולא קביל מיניה ר' עקיבא. ופשט ליה נמי דוולדי מלאכות כמלאכות דמיין דחייב על כל אחת ואחת ולא קביל מיניה:
notes.en: [A footnote in the printed edition: In our Gemara the reading is Rabba; see Tosafot, s.v. “Amar Rabba”; according to our master’s reading, Rava, it is resolved.] Rava: From where do I say it? That with intentional Shabbat and unwitting labors he asked him whether they are like bodies, and he resolved for him that they are like bodies, so that he is liable for each Shabbat, and Rabbi Akiva did not accept it from him. And he also resolved for him that offshoots of labors are like labors, so that he is liable for each one, and he did not accept it from him.

messages.text: The Sages stated a significant principle with regard to the halakhot of Shabbat: With regard to anyone who forgets the essence of Shabbat, i.e., one who is entirely ignorant that labor is prohibited on Shabbat, and he performed multiple prohibited labors on multiple Shabbatot, he is liable to bring only one sin offering, as there is only a single, comprehensive lapse of awareness.

notes.he: דסבור לא נכתבה שבת בתורה דהיינו העלם זה וזה בידו שגגת שבת ושגגת מלאכות:
notes.en: Who forgets the essence of Shabbat: who thinks Shabbat was not written in the Torah; that is, unawareness of both this and that is in his hand, unwitting about Shabbat and unwitting about labors.

notes.he: על כולן [דחדא] שגגה היא והתם ליכא למימר ימים שבינתיים הויין ידיעה דהא לא ידע לעולם עיקר שבת עד שילמוד:
notes.en: One sin offering: for all of them, since it is a single error. And there one cannot say that the intervening days are awareness, for he never knows the essence of Shabbat until he learns.

notes.dh: דתנן כלל גדול אמרו בשבת כל השוכח עיקר שבת
notes.he: כגון תינוק שנשבה לבין הגוים דלא ידע בשבת בעולם:
notes.en: As we learned: A significant principle they stated with regard to Shabbat: Anyone who forgets the essence of Shabbat: for example, a child taken captive among the gentiles, who never knew of Shabbat at all,

notes.he: אינו חייב אלא חטאת א' לכשיודע לו דהא העלם זה וזה בידו:
notes.en: is liable only one sin offering when it becomes known to him, since unawareness of both this and that is in his hand.

messages.text: With regard to one who knows the essence of the prohibition against labor on Shabbat, and he performed multiple prohibited labors on multiple Shabbatot because he was unaware that those days were Shabbat, he is liable to bring a sin offering for each and every Shabbat, as the intervening days are considered awareness which differentiates between the Shabbatot.

notes.he: שידע שארבעים אבות מלאכות אסורות בשבת אבל אינו יודע שהיום שבת דהיינו שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות ועשה מלאכות הרבה בשבתות הרבה ולא נודע לו בינתיים שחטא:
notes.en: Who knows the essence of Shabbat: who knew that the forty [less one] primary labors are prohibited on Shabbat, but does not know that today is Shabbat; that is, unwitting about Shabbat and intentional about labors. And he performed many labors on many Shabbatot, and it did not become known to him in between that he had sinned.

notes.he: חטאת אחת משום דימים שבינתיים הויין ידיעה לענין שגגת שבת ואינו חייב על כל מלאכה ומלאכה של כל שבת ושבת דהא שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות דהיינו הנה שהיא אחת אבל כגופין דמיין ליכא למימר (פשטו מינה) דנימא דמש"ה חייב על כל שבת דעל כרחיך מסיפא קדייק ואזיל דלית ליה להאי תנא שבתות כגופין דמיין וטעמא דרישא משום דימים שבינתיים הויין ידיעה לחלק:
notes.en: He is liable for each and every Shabbat: one sin offering, because the intervening days are awareness with respect to being unwitting about Shabbat. And he is not liable for each labor of each Shabbat, since it is unwitting about Shabbat and intentional about labors, which is “many that are one.” But one cannot say [the text adds in parentheses: “they resolved from it”] that Shabbatot are like separate entities, so that we would say that is why he is liable for each Shabbat; for perforce [Rabba] goes on to infer from the last clause that this tanna does not hold that Shabbatot are like separate entities, and the reason for the first clause is that the intervening days are awareness to differentiate.

notes.he: שיודע שנצטוה על השבת אבל אינו יודע שהיום שבת ועשה מלאכות הרבה בשבתות הרבה. שלא היה יודע שהוא שבת אבל היה יודע שאלו מלאכות אסורין בשבת דהיינו שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות חייב על כל שבת ושבת בלבד ולא על כל מלאכה משום דפשיטא ליה דשגגת שבתות ימים שבינתים הוויין ידיעה לחלק. והיודע שהוא שבת היום דהוה זדון שבת ועשה מלאכות הרבה בשבתות הרבה בהעלם אחת בשגגת מלאכות חייב על כל אב מלאכה ומלאכה:
notes.en: One who knows the essence of Shabbat: who knows that he was commanded about Shabbat but does not know that today is Shabbat, and performed many labors on many Shabbatot; he did not know that it was Shabbat but knew that these labors are prohibited on Shabbat, which is unwitting Shabbat and intentional labors. He is liable for each Shabbat only, and not for each labor, because it is obvious to him that with unwitting Shabbatot the days in between are awareness to differentiate. And one who knows that today is Shabbat, which is intentional Shabbat, and performed many labors on many Shabbatot during one lapse of awareness, unwitting about the labors, is liable for each primary labor.

messages.text: One who is aware that the day is Shabbat and performed multiple prohibited labors, which he did not know were prohibited, on multiple Shabbatot, is liable to bring a sin offering for each and every primary category of labor that he performed.

notes.dh: היודע שהוא שבת ועשה מלאכות [הרבה] בשבתות הרבה
notes.he: ואותן שעשה בזו עשה בזו דשגג במלאכות הרבה כסבור מלאכה זו מותרת חייב על כל מלאכה ומלאכה על שבת ראשון דהיינו אחת שהיא הנה זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות:
notes.en: One who knows that it is Shabbat and performed [many] labors on many Shabbatot: and those he performed on this one he performed on that one, for he erred about many labors, thinking this labor is permitted. He is liable for each labor on the first Shabbat; that is “one that is many”: intentional about Shabbat and unwitting about labors.

messages.text: But in the latter case, the mishna does not teach that he is liable to bring a sin offering for each act of a primary category of labor that he performed on each and every Shabbat. He is liable to bring one sin offering for each primary category of labor, despite the fact that he performed the act on multiple Shabbatot. This indicates that the different Shabbatot are not considered separate entities.
messages.quote: liable to bring a sin offering for each and every primary category of labor

notes.dh: ואילו חייב על כל מלאכה ומלאכה על כל שבת ושבת לא קתני
notes.he: בהך סיפא גבי זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות דכיון דאותן עצמן שעשה בזו עשה בזו ובהעלם אחד אלמא שבתות לאו כגופין דמיין וה"ל עושה מלאכה אחת כמה פעמים בהעלם אחד ואינו חייב אלא אחת:
notes.en: But “liable for each labor on each and every Shabbat” it does not teach: in this last clause, about intentional Shabbat and unwitting labors. Since the very same labors he performed on this one he performed on that one, and during one lapse of awareness, evidently Shabbatot are not like separate entities, and he is like one who performs one labor several times during one lapse of awareness, who is liable only once.

notes.he: ואילו חייב על כל אב מלאכה של כל שבת ושבת לא קתני:
notes.en: But “liable for each primary labor of each and every Shabbat” it does not teach.

messages.text: Whose opinion is this? If we say it is the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer, say the last clause of that mishna:

notes.he: וכי תימא ר' אליעזר היא דאמר במתניתין חייב על כל אחת ואחת:
notes.en: Whose is this mishna of the “significant principle”? And if you say it is Rabbi Eliezer, who says in the mishna “liable for each and every one,”

messages.text: One who performs multiple prohibited labors subsumed, as subcategories, under one primary category of prohibited labor is liable to bring only one sin offering.

notes.dh: מעין מלאכה אחת אינו חייב אלא אחת
notes.he: דכיון דאב אחד לכולן:
notes.en: Of the type of one labor, he is liable only one: since there is one primary category for all of them.

notes.he: העושה מלאכה הרבה מעין מלאכה אחת דהיינו תולדה ואב אינו חייב אלא חטאת אחת:
notes.en: say the last clause of the mishna of the “significant principle”: One who performs many labors of the type of one labor, that is, a subcategory and a primary category, is liable only one sin offering.

messages.text: And if this were the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer it should state: He is liable to bring a separate sin offering for each of the different subcategories of labors as though they were separate primary categories of labor.

notes.dh: ואי ר' אליעזר היא הא ר' אליעזר מחייב על וולדי מלאכות כמלאכות
notes.he: כדאמר לעיל אלא פשיטא ר' עקיבא היא. הא מתניתין:
notes.en: And if it is Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Eliezer deems one liable for offshoots of labors as for labors, as he said above. Rather, it is obvious that this mishna is Rabbi Akiva.

messages.text: Rather, it is obvious that this mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva. And you can learn from the mishna that when one acts unwittingly in that he did not know it was Shabbat and he acts intentionally in that he knows that these labors are prohibited on Shabbat, it is obvious to Rabbi Akiva that the intervening days are considered awareness of his sin, which serves to differentiate between the Shabbatot and render the individual liable to bring separate sin offerings for each Shabbat. It is for this reason that the mishna states that if one performs multiple labors on multiple Shabbatot because he was unaware that it was Shabbat, he is liable to bring a sin offering for each Shabbat.

notes.he: ממציעתא שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות פשיטא ליה לר"ע דימים שבינתיים הויין ידיעה מדקתני חייב על כל שבת ושבת:
notes.en: And learn from it: from the middle clause, that with unwitting Shabbat and intentional labors it is obvious to Rabbi Akiva that the intervening days are awareness, since it teaches: “Liable for each and every Shabbat.”

notes.dh: דתנן כלל גדול כו' אלא פשיטא ר"ע היא וש"מ ימים שבינתים כו'
notes.he: וא"ת מאי פשיטא ליה להביא ראיה מדבריו וי"ל דסבר רבה כיון דמיבעיא ליה בולדי מלאכות דהיינו העושה מלאכות הרבה מעין מלאכה אחת מיבעיא ליה הסמוכה לה דהיינו יודע שהוא שבת ועשה מלאכות הרבה כו' דהיינו זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות אי שבתות כגופין דמיין או לא:
notes.en: As we learned: A significant principle etc.… Rather, it is obvious that it is Rabbi Akiva, and conclude from it that the intervening days etc. And if you will say: what is so obvious to him, that he brings a proof from its words? One can say that Rabba held: since [Rabbi Akiva] is uncertain about subcategories of labors, which is “one who performs many labors of the type of one labor,” he is [also] uncertain about the clause adjacent to it, which is “one who knows that it is Shabbat and performed many labors” etc., that is, intentional Shabbat and unwitting labors, whether Shabbatot are like separate entities or not.

notes.dh: וש"מ שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות פשיטא ליה
notes.he: לר' עקיבא דימים של בינתים הוייא ידיעה לחלק ולהכי פסיק ותנא והיודע עיקר שבת ועשה מלאכות הרבה בשבתות הרבה חייב על כל שבת ושבת:
notes.en: And conclude from it that with unwitting Shabbat and intentional labors it is obvious to Rabbi Akiva that the days in between are awareness to differentiate; and that is why he rules and teaches: “One who knows the essence of Shabbat and performed many labors on many Shabbatot is liable for each and every Shabbat.”

messages.text: Consequently, it is clear that it is in a case where one acted intentionally in that he knew it was Shabbat and unwittingly in that he did not know that the acts he was performing were prohibited labor, that Rabbi Akiva raises his dilemma, as he is uncertain about whether the Shabbatot are comparable to separate entities.

notes.he: וזדון שבת ושגגת מלאכה הוא דבעא מיניה אי כגופין דמיין לחייב על כל שבת ושבת:
notes.en: And intentional Shabbat and unwitting labor is what he asked him, whether they are like bodies, so as to make him liable for each Shabbat.

messages.text: And Rabbi Eliezer resolved the dilemma for him by stating that the different Shabbatot are comparable to separate entities, and different subcategories of labors are comparable to primary categories of labor, and therefore one is liable for each act. And Rabbi Akiva did not accept either of these resolutions from Rabbi Eliezer.

notes.he: מדלא קתני חייב על כל אב מלאכה של כל שבת וולדי מלאכות נמי לא קביל מיניה כדקתני סיפא מלאכה אחת כו':
notes.en: And he accepted neither of them from him: since it does not teach “liable for each primary labor of each Shabbat”; and the subcategories of labors he also did not accept from him, as the last clause teaches: “[of the type of] one labor” etc.

notes.he: כדחזינן במתניתין דאמר ליה דחייב על כל אחת ואחת ולא קביל מיניה מדחזינן דלא פסקא במתני' דכלל גדול דהא ואילו חייב על כל אב מלאכה ומלאכה של כל שבת ושבת לחייבו על כל שבת ושבת לא קתני אלמא דלא קביל מיניה דשבתות כגופין דמיין ובעא מיניה וולדי מלאכות אי כמלאכות דמיין ופשטא דכי מלאכות דמיין. כדאמרינן לעיל ותרוייהו לא קביל א"ל אביי לרבא אימא איפכא אימא דזדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות פשיטא ליה לר' עקיבא דשבת לאו כגופין דמיין. הואיל ולא תנא דחייב על כל אב מלאכה ומלאכה של כל שבת ושבת:
notes.en: And he resolved it for him, as we see in the mishna that he said to him he is liable for each one. And he did not accept it from him, since we see that it is not ruled in the mishna of the “significant principle”: “liable for each primary labor of each and every Shabbat,” which would make him liable for each Shabbat, it does not teach. Evidently he did not accept from him that Shabbatot are like bodies. And he asked him about offshoots of labors, whether they are like labors, and he resolved that they are like labors, as we said above, and he accepted neither of them. Abaye said to Rava [so Rabbeinu Gershom; the daf reads Rabba]: Say the reverse: say that with intentional Shabbat and unwitting labors it is obvious to Rabbi Akiva that Shabbat is not like bodies, since it does not teach “liable for each primary labor of each and every Shabbat.”

messages.text: @Rabba You cannot prove your claim from the mishna. Actually, I could say to you that in a case where one acts intentionally in that he knows it is Shabbat and unwittingly in that he does not know that his actions are prohibited labors, it is obvious to Rabbi Akiva that Shabbatot are not comparable to separate entities, as it can be inferred from the latter clause of this mishna that one is not liable to bring a separate sin offering for each primary category of labor performed on each individual Shabbat.

notes.he: מדלא קתני על כל מלאכה של כל שבת:
notes.en: Abaye said to him [etc.]: Not like separate entities: since it does not teach “for each labor of each Shabbat.”

messages.text: And it is in reference to a case where one acted unwittingly in that he did not know it was Shabbat and intentionally in that he knew his actions are prohibited labors, that Rabbi Akiva raises his dilemma to Rabbi Eliezer. The dilemma is whether the intervening days are considered awareness to differentiate between the Shabbatot or not.

And Rabbi Eliezer resolved the dilemma for him by stating that the intervening days are considered awareness to differentiate between the Shabbatot. And Rabbi Akiva accepted this resolution from him, due the ruling of the mishna that one who knows the essence of the prohibition against labor on Shabbat and performs multiple prohibited labors on multiple Shabbatot is liable to bring a sin offering for each and every Shabbat.

notes.he: מדתניא מציעתא חייב על כל שבת ושבת וה"ק סיפא דמתני' בהמה כשבת הדין עמך דודאי כזה כן זה:
notes.en: And he accepted it from him: since the middle clause teaches “liable for each and every Shabbat.” And this is what the last clause of the mishna means: “The animal is like Shabbat”: the law is with you, for certainly as with this, so with that.

notes.he: ושגגת שבת וזדון מלאכה הוא דבעא מיניה דימים שבינתים מי הוויין ידיעה לחלק אי לא ופשט ליה. מנדה דשגגת נדה וזדון ביאות ימים שבעה דנדה הויא ידיעה לחלק כדאמר לקמן בסיפא דשמעתין:
notes.en: And unwitting Shabbat and intentional labor is what he asked him: are the days in between awareness to differentiate or not? And he resolved it for him from the menstruating woman: that when he is unwitting about the menstruating woman and intentional about the acts, the seven days of menstruation are awareness to differentiate, as is said below at the end of this discussion.

notes.he: ר' עקיבא ולהכי פסקה במתניתין דכלל גדול דהיודע עיקר שבת דהיינו שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכה ואמר דחייב על כל שבת ושבת:
notes.en: And Rabbi Akiva accepted it from him, and that is why he ruled it in the mishna of the “significant principle”: one who knows the essence of Shabbat, which is unwitting Shabbat and intentional labor, and said that he is liable for each and every Shabbat.

messages.text: And Rabbi Eliezer also resolved his other dilemma for him by stating that subcategories of labors are comparable to primary categories of labor and one is liable for each act, but Rabbi Akiva did not accept this resolution from him.

notes.he: מדתניא סיפא מעין מלאכה אחת כו'. בין אביי ורבה איכא פלוגתא אליבא דר"א בזדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות דלרבה מחייב ליה ר"א תרתי ולאביי אפילו ר"א לא מחייב אלא חדא ועוד דמאי דקאמר רבה דמיבעיא ליה לר"ע קאמר אביי דפשיטא ליה אבל תרוייהו מודו דלר"ע שבתות לאו כגופין דמיין וגבי שגגת שבת אית ליה ימים שבינתיים הויין ידיעה לחלק:
notes.en: But he did not accept it from him: since the last clause teaches “of the type of one labor” etc. Between Abaye and Rabba there is a dispute about Rabbi Eliezer’s view on intentional Shabbat and unwitting labors: according to Rabba, Rabbi Eliezer deems him liable twice, and according to Abaye, even Rabbi Eliezer deems him liable only once. Furthermore, what Rabba says Rabbi Akiva was uncertain about, Abaye says was obvious to him. But both agree that according to Rabbi Akiva Shabbatot are not like separate entities, and that with unwitting Shabbat he holds the intervening days are awareness to differentiate.

notes.he: ולא קביל מיניה כדקאמ' בסיפא במתניתין הבהמה כשבת אלמא לא קביל:
notes.en: And he resolved for him that offshoots of labor etc., and he did not accept it from him, as he says in the last clause of the mishna: “The animal is like Shabbat.” Evidently he did not accept it.

messages.text: In a case where one acts intentionally in that he knows it is Shabbat and unwittingly in that he does not know that his actions are prohibited labors, even Rabbi Akiva holds that the Shabbatot are comparable to separate entities;

notes.dh: רב חסדא אמר זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות אפי' ר"ע ס"ל כגופין דמיין
notes.he: והאי דקתני בכלל גדול גבי שגגת מלאכות היודע שהוא שבת כו' חייב על כל מלאכה ומלאכה של כל שבת ושבת קאמר אע"ג דאותה שעשה בזה עשה בזה ובהעלם אחת אפ"ה חייב דשבתות כגופין דמיין משום הכי קתני בשבתות הרבה:
notes.en: Rav Ḥisda says: With intentional Shabbat and unwitting labors, even Rabbi Akiva holds they are like separate entities: and what is taught in the “significant principle” about unwitting labors, “one who knows that it is Shabbat” etc., means he is liable for each labor of each and every Shabbat. Even though what he performed on this one he performed on that one, and during one lapse of awareness, he is nonetheless liable, since Shabbatot are like separate entities; that is why it teaches “on many Shabbatot.”

messages.text: and when he raises the dilemma to Rabbi Eliezer, it is in reference to a case where one acted unwittingly with regard to Shabbat and intentionally with regard to prohibited labor. And he raises the dilemma in order to clarify whether or not the intervening days are considered awareness to differentiate.

notes.dh: רב חסדא אמר זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכה אפי' ר' עקיבא סבירא ליה דכגופין דמיין
notes.he: ואי קשיא לך והא ואילו על כל אב מלאכה של כל שבת ושבת לא תנא הא לא קשיא דכיון דתנא בזדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות דחייב על כל אב מלאכה ומלאכה ה"ה נמי דחייב על כל שבת ושבת ולעולם סבירא ליה דכי גופין דמיין וכי בעא מיניה שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות דימים שבינתי' מי הוויין ידיעה לחלק ופשט' ליה דהויין וקביל מיניה ופסקה במתניתיה:
notes.en: Rav Ḥisda says: With intentional Shabbat and unwitting labor, even Rabbi Akiva holds that they are like bodies. And if it is difficult for you: But “for each primary labor of each and every Shabbat” it does not teach! This is not difficult: since it teaches about intentional Shabbat and unwitting labors that he is liable for each primary labor, the same applies that he is liable for each and every Shabbat; and in fact he holds that they are like bodies. And when he asked him about unwitting Shabbat and intentional labors, whether the days in between are awareness to differentiate, he resolved for him that they are, and he accepted it from him and ruled it in his mishna.

messages.text: And Rabbi Eliezer resolved the dilemma for him by stating that the intervening days are considered awareness to differentiate the transgressions, and Rabbi Akiva accepted this resolution from him. This is in accordance with the mishna in tractate Shabbat (67b) cited earlier, that one who knows the essence of the prohibition against labor on Shabbat and performed multiple prohibited labors on multiple Shabbatot is liable to bring a sin offering for each and every Shabbat.

notes.he: כדקתני (טעמא כו') מציעתא היודע עיקר שבת כו':
notes.en: And he accepted it from him: as the middle clause teaches: “One who knows the essence of Shabbat” etc.

notes.dh: רב חסדא אמר כו' ופשט ליה ימים שבינתיים הויין ידיעה לחלק כו'
notes.he: כי קמייתי ראיה מיניה אבל לא מק"ו דהא אותיב ר"ע על הק"ו אלא מקבלה חייב על כל אחת ואחת:
notes.en: Rav Ḥisda says etc., and he resolved for him that the intervening days are awareness to differentiate etc.: when he brings a proof from him, it is not from the a fortiori inference, since Rabbi Akiva refuted the a fortiori inference, but from a received tradition that he is liable for each one.

messages.text: And Rabbi Eliezer also resolved Rabbi Akiva’s other dilemma for him by stating that different subcategories of prohibited labors are comparable to primary categories of labor and one is liable for each one separately. But Rabbi Akiva did not accept this resolution from him, due to the final clause of that mishna, which states that one who performs multiple prohibited labors that are subsumed as subcategories under one primary category of prohibited labor is liable to bring only one sin offering.

notes.he: כדקתני סיפא מעין מלאכה אחת כו':
notes.en: But he did not accept it from him: as the last clause teaches: “Of the type of one labor” etc.

messages.caption: What Rabbi Akiva asked Rabbi Eliezer, and what he accepted, according to Rabba, Abaye and Rav Ḥisda (16b)

messages.text: From where do I say that according to Rabbi Akiva each Shabbat is considered a separate entity? This is as it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: דאית ליה לר"ע שבתות כגופין דמיין:
notes.en: From where [do I say it]: that Rabbi Akiva holds that Shabbatot are like separate entities.

notes.dh: אמר רב חסדא מנא אמינא ליה
notes.he: דאפילו ר' עקיבא סבירא ליה דכי גופין דמיין:
notes.en: Rav Ḥisda said: From where do I say it, that even Rabbi Akiva holds that they are like bodies?

messages.text: One who writes two letters on Shabbat during one lapse of awareness is liable, as writing two letters renders one liable for performing the prohibited labor of writing.

notes.dh: מדתניא הכותב ב' אותיות בהעלם אחת חייב בב' העלמות
notes.he: דהויא ידיעה בינתים:
notes.en: As it is taught: One who writes two letters during one lapse of awareness is liable; during two lapses of awareness, that is, there was awareness in between,

messages.text: If he does so in two separate lapses of awareness, e.g., he wrote one letter without realizing it was Shabbat, then became aware that it was Shabbat, and then again became unaware it was Shabbat and wrote a second letter, Rabban Gamliel deems him liable to bring a sin offering and the Rabbis deem him exempt.

notes.he: דאין ידיעה לחצי שיעור ולא מהני ידיעה שבינתיים לחלק שלא יצטרפו:
notes.en: Rabban Gamliel deems him liable: for there is no awareness for a half-measure, and the awareness in between does not serve to differentiate so that they would not combine.

notes.he: כדפרשינן לעיל בפירקין דרבן גמליאל סבר אין ידיעה לחצי שיעור אע"ג דהוי ידיעה בינתים לא מפסקא ידיעה לשיעורא ומצטרפי וחייב:
notes.en: Rabban Gamliel deems him liable: as we explained earlier in this chapter, Rabban Gamliel holds there is no awareness for a half-measure. Even though there was awareness in between, the awareness does not interrupt the measure, and they combine, and he is liable.

notes.he: דקסברי יש ידיעה לחצי שיעור ולא מצטרף שיעורא. קא סלקא דעתא רבן גמליאל כר' עקיבא סבירא ליה דשבתות כגופין דמיין:
notes.en: And the Rabbis exempt him: for they hold there is awareness for a half-measure, and it does not combine into the measure. It enters your mind that Rabban Gamliel holds like Rabbi Akiva, that Shabbatot are like bodies.

messages.text: And Rabban Gamliel concedes that if he wrote one letter on this Shabbat and one letter on another Shabbat he is exempt.

notes.dh: אמר רב חסדא מנא אמינא לה דתניא הכותב כו' ומודה ר"ג שאם כתב כו' פטור
notes.he: מהך לבד לא היינו מייתינן בשבתות כגופין מדחזינן דפטור דאיכא למימר דמיירי בשגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות ולכך פטור דימים שבנתיים הויא ידיעה לחלק דאף על גב דר' גמליאל קאמר אין ידיעה לחצי שיעור דלמא ידיעה כי ההיא מחלקת דאיכא לחלק בין ידיעה לימים שבינתיים ובימים שבינתיים מודה דאינה מצטרפת לכך צריך להביא טעם אחר שזדון שבת יש חשיבות לשבתות להיות כגופין משגגת שבת:
notes.en: Rav Ḥisda said: From where do I say it? As it is taught: One who writes etc. And Rabban Gamliel concedes that if he wrote etc. he is exempt. From this alone we would not prove that Shabbatot are like separate entities, from seeing that he is exempt, since one could say it deals with unwitting Shabbat and intentional labors, and that is why he is exempt: because the intervening days are awareness to differentiate. Even though Rabban Gamliel says there is no awareness for a half-measure, perhaps awareness like that does differentiate, since one can distinguish between [ordinary] awareness and the intervening days, and with the intervening days he concedes that the two do not combine. That is why he must bring another [baraita]: that with intentional Shabbat the Shabbatot have more significance, to be like separate entities, than with unwitting Shabbat.

messages.text: And it is taught in a different baraita:
In the case of one who writes two letters on two Shabbatot, one on this Shabbat and one on that Shabbat, Rabban Gamliel deems him liable and the Rabbis deem him exempt.

notes.he: הא דתניא פטור בזדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות דכיון דשבתות כגופין דמיין גבי זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות (דכיון דשבתות כגופין דמיין) ה"ל כעושה ב' חצאי מלאכות שאינן דומות זו לזו בהעלם אחת שפטור מכולם:
notes.en: And another baraita teaches etc.: That which is taught “exempt” is with intentional Shabbat and unwitting labors: since Shabbatot are like separate entities with intentional Shabbat and unwitting labors, it is like one who performs two half-labors that are not similar to each other during one lapse of awareness, who is exempt for all of them.

messages.text: It enters your mind that Rabban Gamliel holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva.

notes.he: כדמפרש לקמן דליכא למימר דכר"א ס"ל מדקתני ומודה:
notes.en: It enters your mind that Rabban Gamliel holds like Rabbi Akiva: as is explained below, that one cannot say he holds like Rabbi Eliezer, since it teaches “and [Rabban Gamliel] concedes.”

messages.text: Granted, according to my opinion, as I say that in a case where one acts intentionally in that he knows it is Shabbat and unwittingly in that he does not know his actions constitute prohibited labors, even Rabbi Akiva says that the Shabbatot are comparable to separate entities.
messages.quote: if he wrote one letter on this Shabbat and one letter on another Shabbat he is exempt

messages.text: Consequently, that which is taught in the first baraita, that Rabban Gamliel concedes that if one wrote one letter on Shabbat and another letter the following Shabbat he is exempt, can be interpreted as referring to a case where one acts intentionally in that he knows it is Shabbat but unwittingly in that he does not know his actions constitute prohibited labors. Since separate Shabbatot are comparable to separate entities, the two acts do not combine to form the minimal act of writing that would render one liable to bring a sin offering.

notes.dh: והא דתני פטור בזדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות
notes.he: דכיון דשבתות כגופין דמיין גבי זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות הוה ליה כעושה שני חצאי מלאכות שאינן דומות זו לזו בהעלם אחת שפטור מכולם:
notes.en: And that which is taught “exempt” is with intentional Shabbat and unwitting labors: for since Shabbatot are like separate entities with intentional Shabbat and unwitting labors, it is like one who performs two half-labors that are not similar to each other during one lapse of awareness, who is exempt for all of them.

notes.dh: בשלמא לדידי דאמינא זדון שבת כוליה
notes.he: מיתרצי מילתא דרבן גמליאל אדרבן גמליאל דהא תניא פטור בזדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות דשבת כי גופין דמיין וכיון דכגופין דמיין ולא עשה אלא חצי שיעור כתיבה בשבת זו וחצי בשבת אחר הילכך לא מיצטרפי ופטור:
notes.en: Granted, according to me, who say [that with] intentional Shabbat [the text here reads “all of it”], Rabban Gamliel’s statement is reconciled with Rabban Gamliel’s: for it is taught “exempt” with intentional Shabbat and unwitting labors, since Shabbat is like bodies. And since they are like bodies, and he performed only half the measure of writing on this Shabbat and half on another Shabbat, therefore they do not combine and he is exempt. [A mark in the printed text here reads: up to here belongs to daf 16b.]

messages.text: Continues on 17a: Rav Ḥisda explains the second baraita, where Rabban Gamliel deems him liable, as a case of one unwitting with regard to Shabbat and intentional with regard to the labors, since Rabban Gamliel holds that there is no awareness for a half-measure. The Gemara then asks how both baraitot are explained according to the view that Rabbi Akiva holds that separate Shabbatot are considered one entity.
